61. It Is All About The Data

作者：Paul W. Homer

As software developers  we initially understand software as a system of commands, functions, and algorithms. This instruction-oriented view of software aids us in learning how to build software, but it is this very same perspective that starts to hamper us when we try to build bigger systems.

作为软件开发者，我们最初把软件理解为命令、函数和算法系统。这种指令导向的软件观帮我们学习怎么建软件，但正是这个视角在我们试图建更大系统时开始妨碍我们。

If you stand back a little, a computer is nothing more than a fancy tool to help you access and manipulate piles of data. It is the structure of this data that lies at the heart of understanding how to manage complexity in a huge system. Millions of instructions are intrinsically complicated, but underneath we can easily get our brains around a smaller set of basic data structures.

退后一点看，计算机不过是帮你访问和操纵成堆数据的花哨工具。正是这些数据的结构，是理解怎么管理大系统复杂度的核心。数百万条指令本质上复杂，但底下我们能容易地用一小套基本数据结构理解。

For instance, if you want to understand the Unix operating system, digging through the source code line-by-line is unlikely to help. If, however, you read a book outlining the primary internal data structures for handling things like processes and the filesystem, you’ll have a better chance of understanding how UNIX works underneath. The data is conceptually smaller than the code and considerably less complicated.

比如，你想理解 Unix 操作系统，逐行读源码未必有帮助。但如果你读一本概述处理进程和文件系统等事物的主要内部数据结构的书，你就更有机会理解 UNIX 底下怎么工作。数据在概念上比代码小，也简单得多。

As code is running in a computer, the underlying state of the data is continually changing. In an abstract sense, we can see any algorithm as being just a simple transformation from one version of the data to another. We can see all functionality as just a larger set of well-defined transformations pushing the data through different revisions.

代码在计算机里跑时，数据底层状态不断变化。抽象地看，任何算法都可以看作从数据一个版本到另一个版本的简单转换。我们可以把所有功能看作更大一组定义良好的转换，把数据推过不同修订。

This data-oriented perspective—seeing the system entirely by the structure of its underlying information—can reduce even the most complicated system down to a tangible collection of details. A reduction in complexity is necessary for understanding how to build and run complex systems.

这种数据导向的视角——完全通过底层信息结构看系统——可以把最复杂的系统降到一组可触摸的细节。复杂度降低对理解怎么建和运行复杂系统是必要的。

Data sits at the core of most problems. Business domain problems creep into the code via the data. Most key algorithms, for example, are often well understood; it is the structure and relationships of the data that frequently change. Operational issues like upgrades are also considerably more difficult if they affect data. This happens because changing code or behavior is not a big issue, it just needs to be released, but revising data structures can involve a huge effort in transforming the old version into a newer one.

数据在大多数问题的核心。业务领域问题通过数据爬进代码。比如，大多数关键算法通常被很好理解；经常变化的是数据的结构和关系。像升级这样的运营问题如果影响数据也难得多。这是因为改代码或行为不是大事，发布就行，但修改数据结构可能涉及把旧版本转成新版本的巨大努力。

And of course, many of the base problems in software architecture are really about data. Is the system collecting the right data at the right time, and who should be able to see or modify it? If the data exists, what is its quality and how fast is it growing? If not, what is its structure, and where does it reliably come from? In this light, once the data is in the system, the only other question is whether or not there is already a way to view and/or edit the specific data, or does that need to be added?

当然，软件架构很多基础问题其实是关于数据的。系统是否在对的时间收集对的数据，谁应该能看或改它？如果数据存在，它的质量如何、增长多快？如果不存在，它的结构是什么、可靠地从哪来？从这个角度看，数据一旦进系统，唯一另一个问题是是否已经有办法查看和/或编辑特定数据，还是需要加？

From a design perspective, the critical issue for most systems is to get the right data into the system at the right time. From there, applying different transformations to the data is a matter of making it available, executing the functionality, and then saving the results. Most systems don’t have to be particularly complex underneath in order for them to work, they just need to build up bigger and bigger piles of data. Functionality is what we see first, but it’s data that forms the core of every system.

从设计角度看，大多数系统的关键问题是在对的时间把对的数据弄进系统。从那里，对数据应用不同转换只是让它可用、执行功能、然后保存结果的事。大多数系统底下不需要特别复杂就能工作，它们只需要堆起越来越大的数据堆。功能是我们先看到的，但形成每个系统核心的是数据。

62. Make Sure the Simple Stuff Is Simple

作者：Chad LaVigne

Software architects solve  a lot of very difficult problems but we also solve some relatively easy ones. What we don’t want to do is apply a complicated solution to an easy problem. As obvious as that advice sounds, it can be hard follow. People who design software are smart—really smart. The simple problem–complex solution trap can be an easy one to fall into because we like to demonstrate our knowledge. If you find yourself designing a solution so clever that it may become self-aware, stop and think. Does the solution fit the problem? If the answer is no, reconsider your design options. Keep the simple stuff simple. You’ll get plenty of chances to showcase your talent when the difficult problems arise, and they will.

软件架构师解决很多非常难的问题，但也解决一些相对容易的。我们不想做的是把复杂方案用到简单问题上。虽然这建议听起来明显，做起来难。设计软件的人聪明——真聪明。简单问题-复杂方案的陷阱容易掉进去，因为我们喜欢展示知识。如果你发现自己设计的方案聪明到可能要有自我意识了，停下来想想。方案配问题吗？如果答案是不，重新考虑你的设计选项。让简单的东西简单。难题来临时你会有很多机会展示才华——它们会来的。

This doesn’t mean that we shouldn’t implement elegant solutions. It means that if we’re tasked with designing a system that only needs to support selling one type of SKU-based widget, it’s probably a bad idea to design for hierarchies of dynamically configurable products.

这不意味着我们不该实现优雅方案。它意味着如果我们的任务是设计一个只需要卖一种基于 SKU 的小部件的系统，为动态可配置产品的层级做设计可能是个坏主意。

The cost incurred by a complicated solution may seem small, but chances are that it’s larger than you’re giving it credit for. Over-engineering at the architectural level causes many of the same issues as it does at the development level, but the negative effects tend to be multiplied. Poor decisions made at the design level are more difficult to implement, maintain, and—worst of all— reverse. Before moving forward with an architectural decision that exceeds system requirements, ask yourself how difficult it would be to remove after it’s in place.

复杂方案带来的成本可能看起来小，但很可能比你想的大。架构层面的过度工程和开发层面一样导致很多问题，但负面效应往往倍增。设计层面做的差决定更难实现、维护，最糟的是——反转。在继续一个超过系统需求的架构决定前，问问自己：它就位后移除会多难。

The costs don’t stop with the implementation and maintenance of the solution in question. Spending more time than necessary on an easy problem leaves less time for when the complicated issues show up. Suddenly your architecture decisions are creating scope creep and adding unnecessary risk to the project. Your time could be spent much more efficiently making sure no one else is doing that.

成本不止于相关方案的实现和维护。在简单问题上花不必要的时间，复杂问题出现时时间就少了。突然你的架构决定在制造范围蔓延、给项目加不必要风险。你的时间可以更高效地用来确保别人不在那么做。

There’s often a strong desire to justify solutions with a perceived benefit or implied requirements. Remember this: when you try to guess at future requirements, 50% of the time you’re wrong and 49% of the time you’re very, very wrong. Solve today’s problem today. Get the application out the door on time and wait for feedback to generate real requirements. The simple design you create will make it much easier to integrate those new requirements when they arrive. If you beat the odds and your implied requirement becomes a real one on the next release, you’ll already have a solution in mind. The difference is that now you’ll be able to allocate appropriate time for it in the estimate because it’s truly required. Before you know it, you’ve got the reputation of a team that makes good estimates and gets work done on time.

经常有强烈欲望用感知到的好处或隐含需求来证明方案合理。记住：当你试图猜未来需求时，50% 时间你错，49% 时间你非常非常错。今天的问题今天解决。让应用按时出门，等反馈产生真实需求。你创建的简单设计会让那些新需求到来时容易集成。如果你打败概率、隐含需求在下个版本成真，你已经心里有方案了。不同的是现在你能在估算里给它分配合适时间，因为它真被需要。不知不觉中，你就有了一个能做好估算、按时完成工作的团队的名声。

63. Before Anything, an Architect Is a Developer

作者：Mike Brown

Have you heard of a judge who wasn’t a lawyer, or a chief of surgery who wasn’t a surgeon? Even after they get to what some would call the pinnacles of their career, the people holding these occupations are still expected to continue learning the new developments within their respective fields. As software architects, we should be held to the same standards.

你听说过不是律师的法官，或不是外科医生的外科主任吗？即使到了某些人说的职业顶峰，从事这些职业的人仍被期望继续学各自领域的新发展。作为软件架构师，我们应该用同样标准要求自己。

No matter how well designed a solution is, one of the most important factors for determining the success of an implementation is getting the developers to sign on to the game plan. The quickest way to get the developers to sign on is to gain their respect and trust. We all know the quickest way to gain a developer’s trust: your code is your currency . If you can show your developers that you’re not just some pie-in-the-sky daydreamer who can’t code his way out of a paper bag, you’ll hear less grumbling about the hoops you’re “making” them jump through to get data to show on the page when “I can get it done in less time by just binding a dataset to a grid.”

不管方案设计多好，决定实现成功最重要的因素之一是让开发签字同意比赛计划。让开发签字最快的方式是赢得他们的尊重和信任。我们都知道赢得开发信任最快的方式：你的代码就是你的货币。如果你能向开发展示你不是只会空想、连纸袋都钻不出去的白日梦想家，你就会少听到抱怨——关于你「让」他们跳圈来把数据显示到页面上，而「我把数据集绑到网格上更快」。

Even though I’m not required to as part of my job, I will frequently pick up some of the more intricate tasks. This serves two purposes: first it’s fun and helps me to keep my development skills sharp; second, it helps me demonstrate to my developers that I’m not just blowing smoke where the sun doesn’t shine.

虽然我工作不要求，我经常会接一些更复杂的任务。这有两个目的：第一好玩、帮我保持开发技能敏锐；第二，它帮我向开发展示我不是在太阳照不到的地方吹牛。

As an architect, your primary goal should be to create a solution that is feasible, maintainable, and of course addresses the issue at hand. Part of knowing what is feasible in a solution is having knowledge of the effort involved in developing the elements of the solution. Therefore, I propose that if you design it, you should be able to code it .

作为架构师，你的主要目标应该是创建可行、可维护、当然解决眼前问题的方案。知道方案里什么可行，部分在于了解开发方案各元素的工作量。因此我提议：如果你设计了它，你应该能写它。

Mike Brown Mike Brown is a lead software engineer for Software Engineering Professionals, Inc. (http://www.sep.com). He has 13 years of experience in IT, including 8 years’ experience developing enterprise solutions in a wide range of vertical markets. He is a founder of the Indianapolis Alt.NET user group, a charter member of the WPF Disciples, and organizer of the upcoming Indy Arc professional user group.

64. The ROI Variable

作者：George Malamidis

Every decision we make for our projects, be it technology-, processor people-related, can be a viewed as a form of investment. Investments come associated with a cost, which may or may not be monetary, and carry trust that they will eventually pay off. Our employers choose to offer us salaries in the hope that this investment will positively affect the outcome of their venture. We decide to follow a specific development methodology in the hope that it will make the team more productive. We choose to spend a month redesigning the physical architecture of an application in the belief that it will be beneficial in the long run.

我们为项目做的每个决定——不管是技术、流程还是人相关的——都可以看作一种投资。投资关联着成本（可能是也可能不是金钱），并带着它们最终会回报的信任。雇主选择给我们发薪水，希望这个投资会正面影响他们事业的结果。我们决定遵循特定开发方法，希望它让团队更高产。我们选择花一个月重新设计应用物理架构，相信长期会有益。

One of the ways of measuring the success of investments is by rate of return, also known as return on investment (ROI). For example, “we anticipate that by spending more time writing tests, we will have fewer bugs in our next production release.” The cost of the investment in this case is derived from the time spent writing tests. What we gain is the time saved from fixing bugs in the future, plus the satisfied customers experiencing better-behaved software. Let’s assume that currently 10 out of 40 working hours in a week are spent fixing bugs. We estimate that by devoting four hours a week to testing, we will reduce the amount of time spent on fixing bugs to two a week, effectively saving eight hours to invest in something else. The anticipated ROI is 200%, equal to the eight hours we save from bug fixing divided by the four hours we invest in testing.

衡量投资成功的方式之一是回报率，也就是投资回报率（ROI）。比如，「我们预期通过花更多时间写测试，下个生产版本 bug 更少。」这个案例投资成本来自写测试花的时间。我们得到的是未来修 bug 省的时间，加上体验到行为更好软件的满意客户。假设目前一周 40 工作小时里 10 小时修 bug。我们估计每周花 4 小时测试，会把修 bug 时间降到每周 2 小时，有效省 8 小时投到别的地方。预期 ROI 是 200%——等于修 bug 省的 8 小时除以测试投的 4 小时。

Not everything need directly translate in monetary gains, but our investments should result in added value. If, for our current project, time to market is essential to the stakeholders, maybe a bulletproof architecture requiring a lengthy upfront design phase will not offer ROI as interesting as a swift alpha release. By quickly going live, we’re able to adapt to audience reactions that can form the deciding element for the future direction and success of the project, whereas not thoroughly planning can incur the cost of not being able to scale the application easily enough when the need arises. The ROI of each option can be determined by examining its costs and projected profits, and can be used as a base for selection from available options.

不是所有东西都直接转化为金钱收益，但我们的投资应该带来附加值。如果对当前项目，上市时间对干系人至关重要，那需要漫长前期设计阶段的防弹架构，ROI 可能不如快速 alpha 发布有趣。通过快速上线，我们能适应观众反应——这可能形成项目未来方向和成功的决定因素；而不充分规划可能在需求出现时不能足够容易地扩展应用。每个选项的 ROI 可以通过检查成本和预期利润来确定，可以作为从可用选项中选择的基础。

Consider architectural decisions as investments and take into account the associated rate of return; it is a useful approach for finding out how pragmatic or appropriate every option on the table is.

把架构决定看作投资，考虑相关回报率；这是找出桌上每个选项多务实或多合适的有用方法。

George Malamidis George Malamidis is a software engineer working for TrafficBroker in London. Before that, he was a lead consultant and technical lead at ThoughtWorks. He has helped deliver critical applications in a variety of domains, from networking to banking to Web 2.0.

George Malamidis George Malamidis 是伦敦 TrafficBroker 的软件工程师。之前是 ThoughtWorks 的首席顾问和技术负责人。他帮交付了从网络到银行到 Web 2.0 各种领域的关键应用。

65. Your System Is Legacy; Design for It

作者：Dave Anderson

Even if your system is bleeding edge and developed in the latest technology, it will be legacy to the next guy. Deal with it! The nature of software today means things go out of date fast. If you expect your system to go into production and survive, even for a few months, then you need to accept that maintenance developers will need to fix things up. This means several things:

即使你的系统是最前沿的、用最新技术开发的，对下一个人来说它也会是遗产。接受吧！今天软件的本质意味着东西过时快。如果你期望系统上线并存活哪怕几个月，那你需要接受维护开发要修东西。这意味着几件事：

Clarity: It should be obvious what role components and classes perform. •

清晰：组件和类扮演什么角色应该明显。

Testability: Is your system easy to verify? •

可测试性：你的系统容易验证吗？

Correctness: Do things work as designed or as they should? Eliminate • quick and nasty fixes.

正确性：东西按设计还是按应该的工作？去掉快速恶心的修复。

Traceability: Can Ernie the Emergency Bug Fixer—who has never seen • the code before—jump into production, diagnose a fault, and put in a fix? Or does he need an eight-week handover?

可追溯性：紧急修 bug 的 Ernie——从没见过代码的人——能跳进生产、诊断故障、提交修复吗？还是他需要八周交接？

Try to think of a different team opening up the codebase and working out what’s happening. This is fundamental for great architecture. It doesn’t have to be oversimplified or documented to the hilt; a good design will document itself in many ways. The way a system behaves in production can also expose the design. For example, a sprawling architecture with ugly dependencies will often behave like a caged animal in production. Spare a thought for (usually more junior) developers who may have to debug defects.

试着想另一个团队打开代码库、搞清楚在发生什么。这是伟大架构的基础。它不必过度简化或文档到极致；好设计在很多方面会自文档化。系统在生产中的行为也能暴露设计。比如，一个蔓延、依赖丑陋的架构在生产中经常像笼子里的动物。替（通常更 junior 的）可能要调试缺陷的开发想想。

Legacy tends to be a bad word in software circles, but in reality, all software systems should endure the tag. It is not a bad thing, as it may indicate that your system is durable, meets expectations, and has business value. Any software system that has never been called legacy has probably been canned before launch—which is not the sign of a successful architecture.

遗产在软件圈里往往是个坏词，但实际上所有软件系统都该忍受这个标签。这不是坏事，因为它可能表明你的系统持久、满足期望、有业务价值。任何从没被叫过遗产的软件系统很可能上线前就被砍了——那不是成功架构的标志。

Dave Anderson Dave Anderson is a principal software engineer at Belfast software company Liberty IT, which supplies IT solutions for Fortune 100 company Liberty Mutual. Dave has more than 10 years’ experience in the software industry with many leading-edge IT companies across several different industries and countries.

Dave Anderson Dave Anderson 是贝尔法斯特 Liberty IT 的首席软件工程师，这家公司为财富 100 强 Liberty Mutual 提供 IT 方案。Dave 在软件业有 10 多年经验，在多个不同行业和国家的领先 IT 公司工作过。

66. If There Is Only One Solution, Get a Second Opinion

作者：Timothy High

You’ve probably heard this said before. If you’re an experienced architect, you know it’s true: if you can only think of one solution to a problem, you’re in trouble.

你大概以前听过这个。如果你是有经验的架构师，你知道这是真的：如果你对一个问题只能想到一个方案，你就有麻烦了。

Software architecture is about finding the best possible solution for a problem given any number of constraints. It is rarely possible to satisfy all requirements and constraints with the first solution that comes to mind. Generally, tradeoffs must be made by choosing the solution that best satisfies the requirements according to the most critical priorities.

软件架构是在任意数量约束下找问题最佳可能方案。用第一个想到的方案满足所有需求和约束很少可能。通常必须通过选最按关键优先级满足需求的方案来做权衡。

If you only have one solution to the problem at hand, it means that you will have no room to negotiate these tradeoffs. It’s very possible that this one solution will be insatisfactory to the stakeholders of your system. It also means that if priorities are shifted due to a changing business environment, your system may have no room to adapt to new requirements.

如果眼前问题你只有一个方案，意味着你没有谈判这些权衡的空间。这个方案很可能让你系统的干系人不满意。它还意味着如果业务环境变化导致优先级转移，你的系统可能没有空间适应新需求。

Rarely, if ever, is this situation caused by a real lack of options. It is much more likely due to the inexperience of the architect in this particular problem domain. If you know this is the case, do yourself a favor and ask someone more experienced to give you a hand.

这种情况很少是因为真的没选项。更可能是因为架构师在这个特定问题领域没经验。如果你知道是这种情况，帮自己一个忙，请更有经验的人帮你。

A more insidious manifestation of this problem is when an architecture is designed from habit. An architect can be experienced with a single style of architecture (e.g., a three-tier, layered client-server system), but not know enough to recognize when that style doesn’t fit. If you find yourself in the situation where you automatically know the solution, without having done any comparison to other approaches, stop, take a step back, and ask yourself if you can think of another way to do it. If you can’t, you may be in need of some help.

这个问题更阴险的表现是架构从习惯设计出来。架构师可能对单种架构风格有经验（比如三层分层客户端-服务器系统），但不够了解什么时候这种风格不合适。如果你发现自己自动知道方案、没和其他方法比较过，停下来，退一步，问自己能不能想到另一种做法。如果不能，你可能需要帮助。

A friend of mine was once the technical person in charge of a small, but growing, Internet startup. As its user base started growing, so did the load requirements on its system. Performance was going down the tubes, and the company was starting to lose some of its hard-won user base.

我一个朋友曾经是一个小型但成长中互联网创业公司的技术负责人。随着用户群增长，系统负载需求也增长。性能在往管子里掉，公司开始失去辛苦赢来的用户。

So, the boss asked him, “What can we do to improve the performance?”

于是老板问他：「我们能做什么提升性能？」

My friend had the answer: “Buy a bigger machine!”

我朋友有答案：「买台更大的机器！」

“What else can we do?”

「我们还能做什么？」

“Umm…as far as I know, that’s it.”

「嗯……据我所知，就这个。」

My friend was fired on the spot. Of course, the boss was right.

我朋友当场被炒。当然，老板是对的。

67. Understand the Impact of Change

作者：Doug Crawford

A good architect reduces complexity to a minimum and can design a solution whose abstractions provide solid foundations to build upon, but are pragmatic enough to weather change.

好架构师把复杂度降到最低，能设计出抽象提供坚实构建基础、又足够务实经得起变化的方案。

The great architect understands the impact of change—not just in isolated software modules, but also between people and between systems.

伟大架构师理解变化的影响——不仅在孤立软件模块里，还在人之间和系统之间。

Change can manifest in a variety of forms:

变化可以多种形式出现：

Functional requirements change •

功能需求变化

Scalability needs evolve •

可扩展性需求演化

System interfaces are modified •

系统接口被修改

People in the team come and go •

团队人员来来去去

And the list goes on… •

等等……

The breadth and complexity of change in a software project is impossible to fathom upfront, and it’s a fruitless task trying to accommodate every potential bump before it happens. But the architect can play a crucial role in determining whether the bumps in the road make or break a project.

软件项目中变化的广度和复杂度不可能前期测透，试图在每个潜在颠簸发生前容纳它是徒劳的。但架构师可以在决定路上的颠簸是成就还是破坏项目上起关键作用。

The architect’s role is not necessarily to manage change, but rather to ensure that change is manageable.

架构师的角色不一定是管理变化，而是确保变化可管理。

Take, for example, a highly distributed solution that spans many applications and relies on a variety of middleware to glue the pieces together. A change in a business process can cause havoc if the set of dependencies is not correctly tracked or accurately represented in some visual model. The impact downstream is particularly significant if the change affects the data model or breaks existing interfaces, and the existing long-running, stateful transactions must successfully complete under the old version of the process.

比如，一个跨多应用、靠各种中间件粘起来的高度分布式方案。如果依赖集合没被正确跟踪或在某个可视化模型中准确表示，业务流程的变化会造成大破坏。如果变化影响数据模型或破坏现有接口、且现有长时间运行有状态事务必须在旧版流程下成功完成，下游影响尤其显著。

This example may appear extreme, but highly integrated solutions are now mainstream. This is evident in the choice of integration standards, frameworks, and patterns available. Understanding the implications of change in these outlying systems is critical in ensuring a sustainable level of support to your customers.

这个例子可能看起来极端，但高度集成方案现在是主流。从可用的集成标准、框架和模式选择就能看出。理解这些外围系统中变化的影响，对确保给客户可持续的支持水平至关重要。

Luckily, there are many tools and techniques to mitigate the impact of change:

幸运的是，有很多工具和技术缓解变化影响：

Make small, incremental changes •

做小的增量变更

Build repeatable test cases and run them often •

构建可重复测试用例并频繁运行

Make building test cases easier •

让构建测试用例更容易

Track dependencies •

跟踪依赖

Act and react systematically •

系统地行动和反应

Automate repetitive tasks •

自动化重复任务

The architect must estimate the effect of change on various aspects of the project’s scope, time, and budget, and be prepared to spend more time on those areas whose impact would be the greatest as a result of “a bump in the road.” Measuring risk is a useful tool for knowing where your valuable time should be spent.

架构师必须估计变化对项目范围、时间和预算各方面的影响，准备好在「路上颠簸」影响最大的领域花更多时间。衡量风险是知道你宝贵时间该花在哪的有用工具。

Reducing complexity is important, but reduced complexity does not equate to simplicity. The payoff for understanding the type and impact of change on your solutions is immeasurable in the mediumto long-term.

降低复杂度很重要，但降复杂度不等于简单。理解变化的类型和对你方案的影响，中长期回报不可估量。

Doug Crawford Doug Crawford manages a team of middleware developers for a telecommunications company in South Africa. He spent the last 10 years fitting square pegs into round holes, and has been intimately involved on application integration projects in a range of industries: advertising, corporate banking, insurance, and education.

Doug Crawford Doug Crawford 管理南非一家电信公司的中间件开发团队。过去 10 年他一直在把方钉塞进圆孔，深度参与了广告、企业银行、保险、教育等一系列行业的应用集成项目。

68. You Have to Understand Hardware, Too

作者：Kamal Wickramanayake

For many software architects, hardware capacity planning is a topic that lies beyond their comfort zone, yet it remains an important part of the architect’s job. There are a number of reasons why software architects often fail to properly consider hardware, but they mostly have to do with a lack of understanding and unclear requirements.

对很多软件架构师来说，硬件容量规划是超出舒适区的话题，但它仍是架构师工作的重要部分。软件架构师经常没恰当考虑硬件有几个原因，但大多和缺乏理解和不清晰需求有关。

The primary reason we neglect hardware considerations is that we are focused on software and tend to ignore hardware demands. In addition, we are naturally isolated from hardware by high-level languages and software frameworks.

我们忽视硬件考虑的主要原因是我们聚焦软件、倾向忽略硬件需求。此外，高层语言和软件框架天然把我们和硬件隔离。

Unclear requirements are also a factor, as they may change or may be poorly understood. As the architecture evolves, hardware considerations will also change. In addition, our clients may not understand or be able to predict the size of their own user base or system usage dynamics. Finally, hardware is constantly evolving. What we knew about hardware in the past does not apply today.

不清晰需求也是因素，因为它们可能变化或被理解得不好。随着架构演化，硬件考虑也会变。此外，我们的客户可能不理解或不能预测自己用户群大小或系统使用动态。最后，硬件在不断演化。我们过去对硬件的了解今天不适用。

Without hardware expertise, predicting hardware configurations for systems to be developed is highly error prone. To compensate, some software architects use large safety factors. Such safety factors are generally not based on objective assessments or founded in any methodology. In most of the cases, this leads to excessive infrastructure capacities that will not be utilized even in periods of peak demand. As a result, clients’ money is wasted on more hardware than a system will ever need.

没有硬件专业知识，预测待开发系统的硬件配置非常容易出错。为弥补，一些软件架构师用大安全系数。这种安全系数通常不基于客观评估、不基于任何方法论。大多数情况下，这导致即使在高峰需求期也用不上的过度基础设施容量。结果，客户的钱浪费在比系统需要更多的硬件上。

The best defense against poor hardware planning is to work closely with an infrastructure architect. Infrastructure architects, unlike software architects,

对差硬件规划最好的防御是和基础设施架构师紧密合作。基础设施架构师和软件架构师不同，

are specialists in hardware capacity planning, and they should be a part of your team. However, not every software architect has the luxury of working with an infrastructure architect. In such cases there are some things a software architect can do to mitigate errors when planning for hardware.

是硬件容量规划专家，他们应该是你团队的一部分。然而不是每个软件架构师都有幸和基础设施架构师合作。这种情况下软件架构师可以做一些事来缓解规划硬件时的错误。

Drawing on your own past experience can help. You’ve implemented systems in the past, so you have some knowledge of hardware capacity planning—even if it was an afterthought at the time. You can also discuss the topic with your client and convince them to set aside funds for hardware capacity planning. Budgeting for capacity planning can be much more cost effective than buying more hardware than you need. In this case, horizontal scalability is the key—adding hardware as needed rather than overbuying in the beginning. To make a horizontal strategy work, software architects need to constantly measure capacity and isolate software components to execute in performancepredictable environments.

利用你自己过去的经验有帮助。你过去实现过系统，所以有一些硬件容量规划知识——即使当时是事后想法。你也可以和客户讨论这个话题，说服他们留出硬件容量规划资金。为容量规划做预算比买比需要更多的硬件划算得多。这种情况下水平扩展是关键——按需加硬件而不是一开始超买。要让水平策略工作，软件架构师需要不断测量容量、隔离软件组件在性能可预测环境中执行。

Hardware capacity planning is as important as software architecture, and it needs to be given a first-order priority whether you have an infrastructure architect on hand or not. Just as an architect is responsible for establishing the links between business demands and a software solution, she is responsible for envisioning the links between hardware and software.

硬件容量规划和软件架构一样重要，不管你手头有没有基础设施架构师，它都需要被给一阶优先级。正如架构师负责建立业务需求和软件方案之间的联系，她也负责构想硬件和软件之间的联系。

Kamal Wickramanayake Kamal Wickramanayake is an IT and software architect who lives in Sri Lanka. He is TOGAF-certified by The Open Group.

Kamal Wickramanayake Kamal Wickramanayake 是住在斯里兰卡的 IT 和软件架构师。他是 The Open Group 认证的 TOGAF 架构师。

69. Shortcuts Now Are Paid Back with Interest Later

作者：Scot Mcphee

It’s important to remember  when architecting a system that maintenance will, in the long run, consume more resources than initial development of the project. Shortcuts taken during the initial development phase of a project can result in significant maintenance costs later.

架构系统时重要的是记住：长期来看，维护会比项目初始开发消耗更多资源。项目初始开发阶段抄的捷径会导致后来重大维护成本。

For example, you may have been informed that unit tests don’t deliver direct value, and so you tell your developers to skip the rigorous application of them. This makes the delivered system much more difficult to change in the future, and decreases confidence when making those changes. The system will require far more manual testing for a smaller set of changes, leading to brittleness and increased maintenance expenses as well as a design that’s not as appropriate as a fully tested design (let alone a test-first design).

比如，你可能被告知单元测试不带来直接价值，所以你告诉开发跳过严格应用它们。这让交付的系统未来难改得多，改的时候信心也下降。系统对更小改动需要远多的手动测试，导致脆弱和维护费用增加，以及设计不如完全测试过的设计（更别提测试先行设计）合适。

A serious architectural mistake is to adapt an existing system for a purpose that it is not fit for, on the basis that using an existing system somehow reduces costs. For example, you might find yourself utilizing BPEL architectural components coupled with database triggers to deliver an asynchronous messaging system. This might be done or insisted upon for reasons of convenience or because that is the architecture known to you or the client. But a messaging architecture should have been selected in the first instance after requirements made it clear, it was a necessary component. Poor decisions made at the inception of a project make it much more expensive to re-architect the system to meet new requirements.

一个严重架构错误是：基于「用现有系统 somehow 降本」的理由，把现有系统改成它不适合的用途。比如，你可能发现自己在用 BPEL 架构组件加数据库触发器来交付异步消息系统。这么做可能是因为方便，或因为那是你或客户熟悉的架构。但消息架构应该在需求明确后第一时间选，它是必要组件。项目初期做的差决定让重新架构系统满足新需求贵得多。

In addition to avoiding shortcuts during the initial development phase, it’s also important to correct poor design decisions as quickly as they are discovered. Poorly designed features can become the foundation for future features, making corrective action later even more costly.

除了在初始开发阶段避免捷径，尽快纠正差设计决定也很重要。差设计的功能可能成为未来功能的基础，让以后纠正更贵。

For example, if you discover that inappropriate libraries were selected for some underlying functionality, they should be replaced as soon as possible. Otherwise, the effort to make them fit evolving requirements will result in additional layers of abstractions, each designed to hide the poor fit of the previous layer. You are building yourself a ball of tangled twine, tack, and sticky tape and with every layer you add, it is harder to unravel. This results in a system that is resistant to change.

比如，如果你发现某些底层功能选了不合适的库，应该尽快替换。否则，让它们适应演化需求的努力会导致额外抽象层，每层都设计来隐藏前一层的不合适。你在给自己缠一团麻绳、图钉和胶带，每加一层，就更难解开。结果是一个抗拒变化的系统。

As an architect, whenever you encounter an architectural problem or design flaw, insist that it be rectified now, when it is cheapest to fix. The longer you leave it to drag out, the higher the interest payment is.

作为架构师，每当遇到架构问题或设计缺陷，坚持现在就纠正——现在是修最便宜的时候。拖得越久，利息付得越高。

Scot Mcphee Scot Mcphee is an Australian software developer and architect with more than 15 years of experience coding and designing applications. Over the last eight years, he’s worked mostly within the J2EE stack.

Scot Mcphee Scot Mcphee 是澳大利亚软件开发者和架构师，有 15 年以上编码和设计应用经验。过去 8 年他主要在 J2EE 技术栈内工作。

70. "Perfect" Is the Enemy of "Good Enough"

作者：Greg Nyberg

Software designers, and architects in particular, tend to evaluate solutions by how elegant and optimum they are for a given problem. Like judges at a beauty contest, we look at a design or implementation and immediately see minor flaws or warts that could be eliminated with just a few more changes or refactoring iterations. Domain models simply beg for one more pass to see if there are any common attributes or functions that can be moved into base classes. Services duplicated in multiple implementations cry out their need to become web services. Queries complain about “buffer gets” and nonunique indexes, and demand attention.

软件设计师——特别是架构师——倾向于用方案对给定问题多优雅、多最优来评估。像选美比赛评委一样，我们看一个设计或实现立刻看到小瑕疵或疣——只要再改几次或重构几次就能去掉。领域模型就是恳求再走一遍看看有没有共同属性或函数可以移到基类。多实现里重复的服务在喊着要变成 Web 服务。查询在抱怨「buffer gets」和非唯一索引，要求关注。

My advice: don’t give in to the temptation to make your design, or your implementation, perfect! Aim for “good enough” and stop when you’ve achieved it.

我的建议：不要屈服于让你的设计或实现完美的诱惑！瞄准「够好」，达到就停。

What exactly is “good enough,” you might ask? Good enough means that the remaining imperfections do not impact system functionality, maintainability, or performance in any meaningful way. The architecture and design hangs together. The implementation works and meets the performance requirements. Code is clear, concise, and well documented. Could it be better? Sure, but it is good enough, so stop. Declare victory and move on to the next task.

你可能问：到底什么是「够好」？够好意味着剩下的瑕疵不以任何有意义方式影响系统功能、可维护性或性能。架构和设计挂得住。实现工作并满足性能需求。代码清晰、简洁、文档良好。能更好吗？当然，但够好了，所以停。宣布胜利，去下一个任务。

The search for perfection in design and implementation leads, in my opinion, to overdesigned and obfuscated solutions that are, in the end, harder to maintain.

在设计和实现中追求完美，在我看来，导致过度设计和混淆的方案，最终更难维护。

A number of the axioms in this book caution designers to avoid unnecessary abstraction or complexity. Why do we have problems keeping things simple? Because we are seeking the perfect solution! Why else would an architect introduce complexity in a workable solution except to address a perceived imperfection in the simpler design?

这本书里很多公理告诫设计师避免不必要抽象或复杂度。我们为什么难以保持简单？因为我们在找完美方案！不然架构师为什么在可行方案里引入复杂度，除非为了解决简单设计里感知到的不完美？

Remember that application development is not a beauty contest, so stop looking for flaws and wasting time chasing perfection.

记住应用开发不是选美比赛，所以别找瑕疵、别浪费时间追完美。

Greg Nyberg Greg Nyberg is currently an independent J2EE computer consultant with 18 years’ experience designing, building, testing, and deploying large, high-volume, transactional applications such as reservation systems, call centers, and consumer websites. He is the author of the WebLogic companion workbook for Enterprise JavaBeans , Third Edition, (O’Reilly), and the lead author of the book Mastering WebLogic Server (Wiley).

Greg Nyberg Greg Nyberg 目前是独立 J2EE 计算机顾问，有 18 年设计、构建、测试和部署大型高吞吐事务应用经验，比如预订系统、呼叫中心、消费者网站。他著有 Enterprise JavaBeans 第三版 WebLogic 配套练习册（O'Reilly），是 Mastering WebLogic Server（Wiley）的主要作者。
